findings.title: Invoice submitters are not authenticated
findings.rationale: The documentation explicitly states that the workflow relies solely on a submitter name embedded in the uploaded invoice document and that submitters are "not otherwise authenticated." This is a documented absence of any authentication control for a workflow that makes financial approval decisions, allowing any party who can submit a file to impersonate an approved submitter. This fails the requirement that authentication for access be established and documented. [Status: documented, confidence: high]
findings.evidence_quote: "The submitter field is a value in the uploaded document; submitters are not otherwise authenticated to the workflow."

findings.title: Full HTTP request and response bodies, including invoice contents, are logged to an observability service
findings.rationale: The system logs complete HTTP request and response bodies for requests and tool calls to an external observability service. Given that user invoices are submitted as JSON over HTTP and contain financial details, those bodies will include the full invoice contents. This means sensitive invoice data is written into application/observability logs and exported to a third-party service, rather than being redacted or excluded, which conflicts with the requirement to keep sensitive data out of logs. [Status: inferred from documentation, confidence: medium-high]
